record.paper_title: Selected Open Problems in Discrete Geometry and Optimization
record.original_question: Let S be a finite set of line segments in R^d. Suppose that for every two distinct segments s' and s'' in S, there exist two distinct parallel supporting hyperplanes H' and H'' of the convex hull of the union of all segments in S such that s' lies in H' and s'' lies in H''. Must the number of segments satisfy |S| <= 2^(d-1)?

evidence.quote: Question 1. Suppose S is a set of segments in Rd such that for every s0, s00 in S with s0 not equal s00 there are different parallel supporting hyperplanes H0, H00 of the convex hull of the union of the segments, such that s0 lies in H0 and s00 lies in H00. Then is it true that |S| <= 2d-1?

artifact.self_contained_problem: Let $d \geq 2$ be an integer and let $S$ be a finite set of (closed) line segments in $\mathbb{R}^d$. Let $C$ denote the convex hull of the union $\bigcup_{s \in S} s$. A hyperplane $H \subset \mathbb{R}^d$ is called a supporting hyperplane of $C$ if $H \cap C \neq \emptyset$ and $C$ lies entirely in one of the two closed half-spaces bounded by $H$. Assume that for every pair of distinct segments $s', s'' \in S$, there exist two distinct parallel supporting hyperplanes $H'$ and $H''$ of $C$ such that $s' \subset H'$ and $s'' \subset H''$. Prove or disprove: under these hypotheses, $|S| \leq 2^{d-1}$.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is a conjecture of Makai and Martini that the maximum number of pairwise antipodal segments in $\mathbb{R}^d$ is $2^{d-1}$. It has been verified in $\mathbb{R}^3$ (the bound $|S|\le 4$ is sharp), and partial results exist for higher dimensions, but the general conjecture for all $d$ appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: On the number of antipodal or strictly antipodal pairs of segments
status_evidence.snippet: Makai and Martini conjectured that k(d) = 2^(d-1); proved n ≤ 4 in R^3 for pairwise antipodal segments, sharp.
status_evidence.claim: The d=3 case is settled; the conjecture for general d is the open Makai–Martini conjecture.

status_evidence.title: Large antipodal families
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses bounds on antipodal families of segments and affine subspaces, referencing the Makai–Martini conjecture.
status_evidence.claim: Conjecture is open in general dimension, only partial bounds known.
